# Model provider jurisdictions

Where each model provider processes your data, and — just as importantly — what that claim actually rests on.

Lunos itself is self-hosted: it runs on infrastructure you provide, and there is no Lunos-operated service in the data path. The only data that leaves your infrastructure goes to the model provider you configure. This page is about _those_ providers.

## How to read this

A provider being "EU" can mean two very different things, and conflating them is how sovereignty claims become misleading:

- **Processing location** — your request data is processed on infrastructure in the EU.
- **Legal entity** — the vendor is an EU-registered company. This says nothing about where data is processed.

Only providers where **both** hold are listed as EU below. Where a provider rests on just one, the table says which one.

**"Depends on configuration"** is not a hedge. Hyperscalers such as Azure, AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex can all run in the EU, and all default to a non-EU region. Whether a given deployment is EU-resident is a choice the deployer makes, not a property of the provider — so these are never reported as EU automatically. The residency controls treat them as non-EU unless the deployment demonstrates otherwise.

**Gateways** (OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, and similar) route onward to other providers. They have no jurisdiction of their own — the effective jurisdiction is whatever they route to, which may vary per request.

## EU-resident providers

| Provider   | Region | Claim rests on        | What is actually true                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------- | ------ | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hetzner`  | EU     | Entity and processing | Hetzner Online GmbH is a German company; its inference offering runs on its own German infrastructure. Reached through the generic openai-compatible plugin.                                                                                                     |
| `mistral`  | EU     | Entity and processing | Mistral AI is a French company and its own API serves EU-hosted inference. Note this is the direct Mistral API only — Mistral models served via Azure or Bedrock inherit that platform's region instead, and are covered by the `azure` / `amazon-bedrock` rows. |
| `ovhcloud` | EU     | Entity and processing | OVHcloud is a French company; AI Endpoints run in its EU data centres. Reached through the generic openai-compatible plugin.                                                                                                                                     |
| `scaleway` | EU     | Entity and processing | Scaleway is a French company (Iliad group); its Generative APIs run in French data centres. Reached through the generic openai-compatible plugin, not a dedicated one.                                                                                           |

### Using one of these

No plugin or extra configuration is needed — these providers ship in the default model catalog. Set the provider's API key and select one of its models:

```sh
export SCALEWAY_API_KEY=...   # Scaleway (France)
export OVHCLOUD_API_KEY=...   # OVHcloud (France)
export HETZNER_API_KEY=...    # Hetzner (Germany)
export MISTRAL_API_KEY=...    # Mistral (France)
```

Then list what that provider currently offers and pick a model from it:

```sh
lunos models scaleway
```

## Depends on your configuration

| Provider                   | Region                   | Claim rests on           | What is actually true                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `amazon-bedrock`           | Depends on configuration | Deployment configuration | AWS is a US entity; Bedrock processing follows the AWS region in use. eu-_ regions are available. Beware cross-region inference profiles, which can route a request outside the region you selected.<br><br>**To get EU:** Set AWS_REGION to an eu-_ region (e.g. eu-central-1, eu-west-1) and avoid cross-region inference profiles.                                                                                                                  |
| `azure`                    | Depends on configuration | Deployment configuration | Microsoft is a US entity, but Azure OpenAI processing location follows the resource's region. EU regions exist and are a genuine option; the region comes from the endpoint URL the deployment is pointed at, so residency is the deployer's choice, not a property of this provider.<br><br>**To get EU:** Create the Azure OpenAI resource in an EU region (e.g. swedencentral, francecentral, germanywestcentral) and use that resource's endpoint. |
| `azure-cognitive-services` | Depends on configuration | Deployment configuration | Same as `azure`: processing follows the Cognitive Services resource's region, chosen at provisioning time.<br><br>**To get EU:** Provision the Cognitive Services resource in an EU region.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `google-vertex`            | Depends on configuration | Deployment configuration | Google is a US entity; Vertex AI processing follows the configured location. europe-_ locations are available.<br><br>**To get EU:** Set the Vertex location to a europe-_ region (e.g. europe-west4).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `google-vertex-anthropic`  | Depends on configuration | Deployment configuration | Anthropic models served through Vertex AI; processing follows the configured Vertex location, as for `google-vertex`.<br><br>**To get EU:** Set the Vertex location to a europe-\* region.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `nebius`                   | Depends on configuration | Legal entity only        | Nebius Group N.V. is registered in the Netherlands following its separation from Yandex, and operates EU data centres — but it also operates elsewhere, and the corporate history warrants stating the entity claim rather than an unqualified EU-processing one. Verify the serving region before relying on this for residency.<br><br>**To get EU:** Confirm with Nebius which region serves your account.                                          |
| `sap-ai-core`              | Depends on configuration | Legal entity only        | SAP SE is a German company, so the entity claim is solid. Processing location depends on which BTP region the deployment uses, and SAP operates non-EU regions too — so the entity being European does not by itself make the data EU-resident.<br><br>**To get EU:** Provision SAP AI Core in an EU BTP region (e.g. eu10/eu11).                                                                                                                      |
| `snowflake-cortex`         | Depends on configuration | Deployment configuration | Snowflake is a US entity; Cortex inference runs in the account's deployment region, which may be an EU region. Cross-region inference must be disabled for the region choice to hold.<br><br>**To get EU:** Use a Snowflake account in an EU deployment region and disable cross-region inference.                                                                                                                                                     |

## No jurisdiction of their own

| Provider                | Region           | Claim rests on          | What is actually true                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cloudflare-ai-gateway` | Not determinable | Inherited from upstream | A proxy. The effective jurisdiction is that of the upstream provider it routes to, plus Cloudflare edge handling in transit. Evaluate the upstream provider's row, not this one.                                                                        |
| `dynamic-provider`      | Not determinable | User-supplied endpoint  | Provider defined at runtime from user configuration. Jurisdiction cannot be determined statically.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `gateway`               | Not determinable | Inherited from upstream | Vercel AI Gateway. Jurisdiction is that of the upstream provider it routes to.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `llmgateway`            | Not determinable | Inherited from upstream | Aggregating gateway. Jurisdiction is that of the upstream provider it routes to.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `openai-compatible`     | Not determinable | User-supplied endpoint  | Generic adapter for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Jurisdiction is whatever the configured baseURL resolves to — including EU providers such as Scaleway, OVHcloud and Hetzner, which have their own rows. Cannot be determined from the plugin alone. |
| `opencode`              | Not determinable | Inherited from upstream | Upstream opencode's hosted gateway. Jurisdiction is that of the upstream provider it routes to.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `openrouter`            | Not determinable | Inherited from upstream | Routes to many upstream providers, selected per request and possibly per availability. No single jurisdiction can be asserted.                                                                                                                          |

## Scope and limits of this page

- This records **where data is processed**, not a data-protection assessment. A provider being EU-resident does not by itself discharge GDPR obligations — you still need the appropriate agreement with that provider.
- Sub-processors are not enumerated. A provider processing in the EU may still rely on sub-processors; check its own documentation.
- Entries are maintained on the project's best current understanding and are not a substitute for the provider's own contractual commitments. Where something could not be verified, the table says so rather than guessing.

Corrections are welcome — the source of truth is `packages/core/src/jurisdiction.ts`, and a correction there regenerates this page.
